blocks.content: Your local repository lives on your machine. GitHub lets you store it online so it is backed up and accessible from anywhere.
First, create a new repository on GitHub.
Log in, click the + icon, select New repository, give it a name, and click Create repository. Leave the README option unchecked, since your local project already has commits.

blocks.alt: GitHub new repository form with name field filled in and Create repository button

blocks.content: Now connect your local project to GitHub:
origin is the name for this connection. It is just a label — but origin is the universal convention for the primary remote.
Your local repository now knows where GitHub is. Nothing has been uploaded yet.
